sense: a list at the back of a book

terms.gloss: a list, catalogue, table of contents
evidence: Quint. 10.1.57: indicem certē ex bibliothēcā sūmptum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A list of contents is classical (Quintilian, Seneca, Pliny); the alphabetical index at the back of a book is modern, and Morgan–Owens gives index rērum for it. The word’s other senses: a pointer, the forefinger (digitus index), an informer, a book’s title (see title, of a book).

phrases.latin: Fungar indicis partibus, atque etiam quō sint ōrdine scrīptī nōtum tibi faciam.
phrases.english: I’ll play the part of an index, and tell you too in what order they were written.

sources: Lewis & Short: index
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. parts: index.
